exercise.name: Bodyweight Bent Over Rear Delt Fly

reference.title: Bodyweight Bent Over Rear Delt Fly
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise the arms, breathe in as you lower; keep the trunk braced.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Body weight (arms only); add light dumbbells or a band when it gets easy
prescription.frequency: 2-4 times a week (also as a warm-up)
prescription.progression: More reps and longer squeezes, then dumbbell or band reverse flies

cues.text: Feet hip width, knees soft, hinge at the hips until the trunk is nearly parallel to the floor with a flat back. Arms hang under the shoulders, palms facing each other.
Breathe out and sweep the arms out to the sides with soft elbows, leading with the backs of the hands.
Arms about level with the back; squeeze the shoulder blades together and hold briefly.
Lower slowly back under the shoulders; keep the trunk still.
Stay in the hinge, reset and repeat.

mistakes.fix: Push the hips back, keep the chest long; stand a little more upright if needed.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows and pulling back (rowing)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow bend fixed and move the arms out to the sides.
Keep the trunk still; slow the arms down.
Draw the shoulder blades back and down.

kinematics.norm: Nearly parallel to the floor, flat back (clinical opinion)
From arms hanging to about level with the back; prone horizontal abduction tested at about 100 degrees of abduction (Reinold 2007)
Palms facing each other at the bottom; a neutral hand position gave more posterior deltoid activity than pronated on a reverse fly (Schoenfeld 2013)

sources.title: GymVisual 14318, Bodyweight Bent Over Rear Delt Fly, video (movement reference)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The bent-over position loads the low back even without weights: keep the back flat and take breaks if it tires.
modify: Low-back discomfort: do it lying face down on a bench or the floor (prone T raise), or seated bent over the knees.
Hamstring tightness: bend the knees more.
regressions: Prone T raise on the floor.
progressions: Slower 3 s lowering with a 2 s squeeze.
